note: Per-profile career-project list. One REAL flagship project per real (non-consulting) company, within that company's date range, each chosen because it spans the platform, backend, and data/operations layers in a single delivery path (so the resume can claim all of them from one coherent project). For the 2 MOST RECENT companies (isRecentTwo:true) we keep company info only - bullets are tailored live at generation. For older companies we ship ready-made bullets, pitched at the seniority appropriate to that point in the career. Consulting companies (consulting:true) store NO project - at generation their engagements are pulled from shared.json (industry-matched entry + 1 more arbitrary). Descriptions are plain-terms, one paragraph. NOTE: no company on this profile currently carries consulting:true in Experiment/bullets/rowland_sipola.json, so shared.json engagements are not used; Deloitte is the natural candidate if that is ever turned on.

projects.description: An Internal Developer Platform is the paved road application teams use instead of hand-building their own infrastructure. An engineer picks a template, and the platform provisions the cloud resources behind it as code, wires the service into a standard Kubernetes release path with health checks and progressive rollout, and turns on monitoring, tracing, and alerting from day one - so a new service reaches production in hours rather than days, with secure-by-default settings already applied. It touches the front end (the self-service catalog and dashboards teams work in), the back end (the reusable Python platform services and automation that do the provisioning), and the infrastructure/operations layer (Kubernetes, Terraform, cross-cloud integrations with Azure and AWS, and the observability that keeps it all healthy). One platform, all three layers.

projects.flagshipProject: Secure-by-default multi-region Kubernetes platform + DevSecOps control plane
projects.description: This is the platform that lets an enterprise ship software quickly without shipping vulnerabilities with it. Every code change moves through a CI/CD pipeline that scans it several ways - source code, running app, dependencies, secrets, infrastructure definitions, and a bill of materials - before it is allowed near production. What survives lands on a multi-region Kubernetes platform delivered by GitOps, with zero-trust networking, private endpoints, encryption in transit and at rest, and disaster-recovery runbooks with defined RPO/RTO targets. Around it sits continuous compliance: cloud baselines checked against CIS benchmarks, SOC 2 and ISO 27001 evidence collected automatically, and policy-as-code guardrails that let product teams self-serve infrastructure without stepping outside policy. It touches the backend/delivery layer (the pipelines and the services they deploy), the infrastructure layer (multi-region Kubernetes, IaC, and cloud landing zones), and the security/operations layer (the scanning, compliance automation, observability, SLOs, and error budgets).

projects.flagshipProject: Hardened Linux production estate + automated patch & log pipeline
projects.description: Tellic's production estate is the set of Linux servers that actually run the company's web, mail, and messaging services, plus everything that keeps them safe and observable. A request lands on a hardened Ubuntu/CentOS host behind a firewall and VPN gateway; intrusion detection watches the traffic; the service itself runs in a container shipped by an automated deployment pipeline; and every log line the host emits is shipped to a central search cluster so anything unusual can be found in minutes instead of days. It touches the infrastructure layer (the server fleet, networking, firewalls, and IDS/IPS), the backend/delivery layer (containerized services, configuration management, and the automated patch pipeline that keeps them CVE-clean), and the data/operations layer (centralized log aggregation and search used for security and reliability investigations).
bullets: Managed and hardened Linux (Ubuntu / CentOS) fleets of web, mail, and messaging servers while maintaining 99.9% uptime across production services.
Deployed OpenVPN gateways, iptables firewalls, and Snort IDS/IPS to reduce external intrusion attempts within six months.
Containerized internal services with Docker and automated deployments with Ansible, reducing environment setup from days to hours per service.
Built an automated patch pipeline using Bash, Ansible, and cron, bringing servers to CVE compliance within 72 hours of critical releases.
Centralized log aggregation with ELK (Elasticsearch, Logstash, Kibana), reducing time to detect security anomalies from days to hours.

projects.flagshipProject: Self-service deployment platform + real-time listing pipeline
projects.description: Zillow's core search product depends on two things working together: engineers being able to ship safely, and property listings being fresh. The deployment platform is what engineers use to get a service from their laptop into production - it provisions an environment, builds a container, and rolls it out - so releases go from bi-weekly to daily without environment-parity surprises. The listing pipeline is what keeps the data behind search current: as new and updated listings arrive they stream through a message bus into the databases that power search results the same day. It touches the infrastructure layer (the provisioning, container platform, and secrets management behind every service), the backend layer (the services and queries serving high-traffic search), and the data layer (the streaming pipeline that keeps listings fresh).
bullets: Built a self-service deployment platform using Python, Jenkins, and EC2 for 60+ engineers; reduced environment provisioning from days to hours and lowered platform support load.
Migrated core services from bare-metal EC2 to Docker and ECS, accelerating releases from bi-weekly to daily and eliminating environment parity bugs.
Centralized secrets management with AWS KMS and supported SOC 2 Type I compliance readiness.
Built a real-time property listing pipeline using Kafka, Python, and PostgreSQL, supporting 99.9% uptime and same-day data freshness for Zillow's core search product.
Optimized PostgreSQL queries across high-traffic services using indexing and EXPLAIN ANALYZE, reducing API p99 latency and monthly RDS spend.
Introduced Terraform for AWS IaC, mentored mid-level engineers, and reduced manual provisioning errors.

projects.flagshipProject: Search indexing pipeline + Borg/Borgmon serving reliability
projects.description: Google Search only feels instant because two systems stay healthy: the pipeline that turns crawled pages into a fresh index, and the cluster machinery that serves queries from it. The indexing pipeline takes documents through distributed processing jobs so a newly crawled page shows up in results within a sub-second freshness target, at petabyte scale. The serving side runs on Google's internal cluster scheduler with a monitoring framework watching every job - deciding where jobs run, how much compute they get, and when to page a human. It touches the data layer (the MapReduce/Flume indexing pipeline), the backend layer (the RPC libraries and latency-sensitive serving path), and the infrastructure layer (job scheduling, monitoring, alerting, and on-call for a tier-1 cluster).
bullets: Built data pipeline components for Google Search indexing using MapReduce and Flume, supporting sub-second document freshness SLOs at petabyte scale.
Rewrote flapping-detection logic in the Borgmon monitoring framework, reducing false-positive on-call pages.
Tuned Borg job scheduling for a tier-1 serving cluster, improving CPU utilization and freeing compute capacity for reallocation.
Fixed critical p99 latency regressions in an internal Go RPC library used by 12+ services; shipped with full unit and integration test coverage.
Owned Search backend on-call using Oncall and Buganizer; authored postmortems that eliminated recurrence of top incident classes within one quarter.
